record.context_brief: quantum description of dark-atom nuclear interactions
record.original_question: How can one construct a proper quantum-mechanical description of the nuclear interaction between dark atoms and ordinary nuclei, in a regime without the small parameters used in ordinary atomic physics, so that it can quantitatively analyze anomalous-isotope formation after Big Bang nucleosynthesis, dark-atom capture by stars, effects on stellar nucleosynthesis, and the dark-atom interpretation of the DAMA/NaI and DAMA/LIBRA annual-modulation results?

evidence.quote: The basic open problem of the dark atom hypothesis is related to the proper quantum-mechanical description of the nuclear interaction of dark atoms.

Development of the proper quantum mechanical description of dark atom interaction with nuclei is necessary for analysis of dark atom formation of anomalous isotopes after BBN, of effects of dark atom capture by stars and effects in stellar nucleosynthesis, as well as for the proof of dark atom interpretation of DAMA/NaI and DAMA/LIBRA results.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the hypothesis that dark matter consists of "dark atoms": neutral bound states formed by a hypothetical stable lepton-like particle X of electric charge −2n (n a positive integer) with n primordial ⁴He nuclei, held together by Coulomb attraction. Because the helium constituents carry unshielded nuclear charge and the binding scale is comparable to nuclear scales, the small parameters that justify perturbative or Born–Oppenheimer treatments in ordinary atomic physics (small ratio of electronic to nuclear scales, weak coupling, large separation of length scales) are not available.

Develop a fully quantum-mechanical description of the interaction of such a dark atom with an ordinary atomic nucleus of charge Z and mass number A that:

1. Treats the system as a coupled few-body problem incorporating both the long-range Coulomb interaction between the constituents of the dark atom and the target nucleus and the short-range strong nuclear interaction between the helium component and the target nucleus.
2. Produces an effective dark-atom–nucleus interaction potential exhibiting a dipole Coulomb barrier that prevents fusion of the helium component with the target nucleus, together with the bound-state spectrum (if any) supported by this potential.
3. Is quantitative enough to predict (a) the rate of formation of anomalous isotopes via dark-atom capture by nuclei after Big Bang nucleosynthesis, (b) the rate and effects of dark-atom capture by stars and modifications of stellar nucleosynthesis, and (c) the radiative capture cross sections of dark atoms on Na and I nuclei in the keV recoil-energy range relevant to the annual-modulation signals observed by DAMA/NaI and DAMA/LIBRA.

Construct such a description and use it to determine whether the dark-atom hypothesis can simultaneously satisfy the cosmological and astrophysical constraints in (a)–(b) while reproducing the DAMA modulation amplitude in (c).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Khlopov, Mayorov and collaborators, 2024–2025) has made significant progress: numerical three-body Schrödinger-equation models of OHe/XHe dark-atom interaction with Na and other nuclei have been constructed, yielding an effective potential with a dipole Coulomb barrier and a single shallow bound state of order −2 keV with Na, consistent with the DAMA energy window. However, a fully self-consistent treatment incorporating the nuclear interaction without small-parameter approximations, and quantitative predictions for anomalous-isotope formation after BBN and stellar nucleosynthesis effects, remain incomplete; the program is acknowledged as ongoing.

status_evidence.title: Quantum Mechanical Numerical Model for Interaction of Dark Atom with Atomic Nucleus of Matter
status_evidence.snippet: Solving the three-body Schrödinger equation, the authors determine the effective dark-atom–Na potential and find a bound state near −2 keV in the 1–6 keV range relevant to DAMA.
status_evidence.claim: Recent quantum-mechanical numerical model addresses the dark-atom–nucleus interaction problem for the DAMA interpretation.

status_evidence.title: Quantum-mechanical numerical model of interaction between dark atom and nucleus of substance
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical three-body model of XHe–nucleus interaction with self-consistent electromagnetic and nuclear couplings.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing 2025 work develops the required quantum-mechanical formalism but does not yet cover BBN and stellar nucleosynthesis predictions.

status_evidence.title: The bound state of dark atom with the nucleus of substance
status_evidence.snippet: Further development of the bound-state analysis of dark atom with substance nuclei.
status_evidence.claim: The problem remains an active research program with incremental advances rather than a complete solution.
